places.name: Brazos Bend State Park
places.coord_point: printed park coordinates on the TPWD page (point type not labelled)
nearby: Needville (town of the park's mailing address)
Houston (45 miles, per the TPWD page)
George Observatory (inside the park)
places.blurb: Brazos River bottomland with the George Observatory inside the park, plus cabins, screened shelters and group sites.
places.status_note: The page flags active alerts (details not printed). Some trails close in wet weather, so ask at the park office.
places.notes: CANDIDATES (ten, from which I chose): Ephemeris, Gazetteer, Meridian, Chartroom, Zenith, Starwheel, Lodestar, Culmination, Vantage, Sightline. CHOSEN: Ephemeris. COORDINATE CONFLICT: TPWD prints 29.371000, -95.631921; the Wikipedia infobox gives 29.37889, -95.59500, about 3.7 km away, so the official point is used per the 2 km rule. COUNTY and ACREAGE are not printed on TPWD; both come from the Wikipedia infobox (Fort Bend County, 4,897 acres). CAMPING: the page says only 'campsites' (tent and RV not specified), plus screened shelters, cabins and group sites; equestrian camping is not printed (the page mentions 13 miles of multiuse horse trails). Reservations are 'highly recommended', not mandatory. Wikipedia names no nearby places with distances.

places.name: Devils River State Natural Area
places.coord_point: Dan A. Hughes Unit, printed coordinates (first unit listed on TPWD; the page does not say which unit holds the headquarters)
nearby: Del Rio (nearest city)
Ciudad Acuna (named alongside Del Rio on TPWD)
Del Norte Unit (printed point about 23 km north of Dan A. Hughes)
places.blurb: Remote desert river country with primitive camps, a group barracks, river paddler camps and a dark sky sanctuary designation.
places.status_note: Closed Tuesday through Thursday. Friday to Sunday the gate opens 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. and the park closes 10 p.m. Reservations are required for either unit. Two active alerts are listed (one screwworm, one park), details not printed.
places.notes: TWO UNITS, printed separately: Dan A. Hughes Unit 29.729917, -100.960168 (used as the point because it is listed first) and Del Norte Unit 29.939694, -100.970206, about 23 km north. The Wikipedia infobox point (29.92301, -100.97033, no source named) sits about 1.9 km from the Del Norte point, so it describes the Del Norte unit; it is not a conflict. DARK SKY: DarkSky's page is titled 'Devils River State Natural Area - Del Norte Unit', designated 2019, category International Dark Sky Sanctuary, address 21715 Dolan Creek Rd, Del Rio. TPWD's dark skies page names the same sanctuary designation. The Black Gap WMA also named by TPWD is outside this row. CAMPING KINDS: primitive sites with no water or electricity (both units), a group barracks with restrooms and showers at Del Norte, and river paddler campsites that need a Devils River Access Permit ($10); I filed the paddler camps under backcountry, which is my approximation. ACREAGE 37,000 is the combined figure printed on TPWD ('37,000-plus acres') and in Wikipedia. Entrance is $5 daily for ages 13 and up. Wikipedia names no other places within 50 miles.

places.name: Galveston Island State Park
places.coord_point: printed park coordinates on the TPWD page (point type not labelled)
nearby: Galveston (the park lies within the city limits)
Gulf of Mexico (the beach frontage)
Galveston Bay (named in the island description)
places.blurb: Gulf beach and bay-side campsites on western Galveston Island, with lodges for rent.
places.status_note: The page flags active alerts (details not printed). No day-use-only notice. Reservations are highly recommended for camping and day use.
places.notes: COORDINATES: TPWD 29.198755, -94.956212 agrees with the Wikipedia infobox 29.19889, -94.95611 to within about 20 m; the printed point is used. COUNTY (Galveston County) and ACREAGE (2,013.1 acres) come from Wikipedia; TPWD prints neither. CAMPING: the page names bay-side and beach-side campsites and lodges for rent, but does not say which campsites are tent or RV sites, and does not say whether the lodges are cabins; the group sites page is linked but not described; primitive and screened shelters are not printed. Beach horseback riding is allowed November through February only, which is a day activity, not equestrian camping. Wikipedia names Galveston Bay, the Gulf of Mexico and the Stewart Mansion (location not stated) without distances.

places.name: Lake Arrowhead State Park
places.coord_point: printed park coordinates on the TPWD page (point type not labelled)
nearby: Wichita Falls (the park is 15 minutes south of it, per TPWD)
Henrietta (Clay County seat, named on TPWD)
Lake Arrowhead reservoir (16,200 acres, per TPWD)
places.blurb: Lakeside park on a 16,200-acre reservoir with electric and water sites, walk-in primitive camping and equestrian camping.
places.status_note: No closure or day-use-only notice printed. Reservations are strongly recommended for camping and day use.
places.notes: COORDINATES: TPWD 33.758578, -98.395201 agrees with the Wikipedia infobox 33.75861, -98.39528 to within about 10 m; the printed point is used. Weather-link coordinates on the TPWD page are not park coordinates and were ignored. COUNTY (Clay) comes from Wikipedia; TPWD prints only Henrietta, the county seat. ACREAGE 524 comes from Wikipedia; TPWD's 16,200 acres is the reservoir, not the park. CAMPING: an RV/electric area of 8 loops of 6 sites (4 pull-through), 19 water-only sites, a primitive walk-in area and an equestrian camping area. The page does not use the phrase 'RV hookups', so rv_hookups is my mapping of the electric and water sites. Group sites are linked but not described; tent, cabins and screened shelters are not printed.

places.name: Longhorn Cavern State Park
places.coord_point: printed park coordinates on the TPWD page (point type not labelled)
nearby: Burnet (the park address town)
Kingsland (Llano County, named as nearest town by Wikipedia)
Inks Lake State Park (TPWD refers campers there)
places.blurb: Hill Country day-use park where the cavern is entered only on paid guided tours. No overnight camping.
places.status_note: Day use only, with no overnight camping. Cave entry is by paid guided tour only (tour prices not printed; the page says 'Contact the Park'). Active alerts are listed (a screwworm notice), details not printed.
places.notes: NO CAMPING: the TPWD page says 'Longhorn Cavern State Park is a day-use only park. There is no overnight camping.' camping is false with an empty kinds list; for camping the page refers visitors to Inks Lake State Park. COORDINATES: TPWD 30.684441, -98.350970 agrees with the Wikipedia infobox 30.68472, -98.35083 to within about 35 m; the printed point is used. An NWS forecast link on the same page carries different coordinates, which are not labelled as park coordinates and were ignored. NEAREST TOWN: the TPWD address is Burnet; Wikipedia names Kingsland as nearest, and I kept Burnet from the official address. COUNTY (Burnet) and ACREAGE (645.62) come from Wikipedia. Dark sky is not mentioned.

places.name: Palmetto State Park
places.coord_point: printed park coordinates on the TPWD page (point type not labelled)
nearby: Gonzales (the park address town)
Luling (northwest of Gonzales, per Wikipedia)
places.blurb: Gonzales County park with 19 tent sites, 17 RV sites, a group site for up to 24 people and an air-conditioned cabin.
places.status_note: The page flags active alerts (text not included); no closure printed. Reservations are advised two to three weeks ahead from March to November.
places.notes: COORDINATES: TPWD 29.596906, -97.585140 and the Wikipedia infobox 29.58722, -97.58222 (no source named) are about 1.1 km apart, inside the 2 km tolerance, so the printed point is used. COUNTY (Gonzales) and ACREAGE (270.3) come from Wikipedia; TPWD prints neither. Wikipedia places the park northwest of Gonzales and southeast of Luling; the TPWD address uses Gonzales. CAMPING: 19 tent sites, 17 RV sites (the page does not print hookups), a secluded group site for up to 24 people, and one air-conditioned cabin for six. Primitive, equestrian and screened shelters are not printed. No dark sky mention.

places.coord_point: printed park coordinates on the TPWD page (point type not labelled)
nearby: Comstock (the park is 9 miles west of it, per Wikipedia)
Del Rio (nearby city, named on TPWD)
Amistad National Recreation Area (adjoins the park, per Wikipedia)
places.blurb: Canyon park with 46 campsites, a historic site, and hiking in the canyon area that requires a guide.
places.status_note: The canyon area can only be hiked with a guide, and Fate Bell Shelter tours need reservations. The page flags active alerts (details not printed).
places.notes: COORDINATES: TPWD 29.700094, -101.312875 is used. The Wikipedia infobox 29.68333, -101.31833 (no source named) is about 1.9 km away, inside the 2 km tolerance. COUNTY (Val Verde) and ACREAGE (2,172.5) come from Wikipedia. Wikipedia gives Comstock as the nearest town, 9 miles (14 km) west of it; TPWD gives Comstock as the mailing city and names Del Rio as the nearby city. CAMPING: 46 campsites, described as 'primitive drive-up sites' and sites 'with water and electricity' (restrooms and showers nearby). The page does not print the words tent or RV hookup; rv_hookups is my reading of 'water and electricity' and needs a human check. Wikipedia names the Seminole Canyon Archeological District (the park is part of it) without a distance.

places.notes: NO PRINTED COORDINATES on the NPS planyourvisit page. The point is the Wikipedia infobox 30.59917, -103.89278 (30 degrees 35 minutes 57 seconds N, 103 degrees 53 minutes 34 seconds W), which is not an NPS coordinate, and the visitor centre's location within the site is not printed. COUNTY (Jeff Davis) and ACREAGE (523) come from Wikipedia; the NPS page prints neither. CAMPING: the NPS page says 'There is no lodging or camping in Fort Davis National Historic Site.' Camping is in the town and at Davis Mountains State Park. The NPS page gives the mailing address as P.O. Box 1379, 101 Lt. Flipper Dr., Fort Davis, TX 79734.

places.name: Sam Houston National Forest
places.coord_point: FOREST CENTRE from the Wikipedia infobox, NOT a district office or campground; no official office or campground coordinates were found
nearby: New Waverly (Sam Houston Ranger District office, 394 FM 1375 West)
Coldspring (Double Lake Recreation Area is about 1 mile south on FM-2025, per Wikipedia)
Cagle Recreation Area (5 miles west of I-45 on FM-1375, per Wikipedia)
places.blurb: Forest about 50 miles north of Houston with lakeside campgrounds, 85 miles of multiple-use trails and a scenic area closed to camping.
places.status_note: Two forest alerts are listed by title only: a Sam Houston National Forest Closure Order and a road-work alert. The official page shows fire danger 'Extreme' on a page last updated July 8, 2025, which is stale.
places.notes: THIS IS A FOREST, SO THE POINT IS A FOREST CENTRE, NOT AN OFFICE. The Wikipedia infobox 30.58444, -95.13250 (no source named) is the only coordinate I found. The official pages print no coordinates for the forest, for the New Waverly district office (394 FM 1375 West, New Waverly, TX 77358, (936) 344-6205) or for any campground, and Double Lake has no article of its own (its link redirects to the forest article). OFFICE COORDINATES NOT FOUND; a geocode of the office address is the next step. ACREAGE: 163,037 from the official page; Wikipedia says 163,045. COUNTY: the official page names Montgomery, San Jacinto and Walker counties and does not say which holds the office. CAMPGROUNDS (the official list shows 10 of 13 results; page 2 was not read): Kelly's Pond Campground (8 tent campsites, official page), Double Lake Recreation Area (family and group camping, per Wikipedia), Cagle Recreation Area (48 electric, fresh-water and sewer spurs, per Wikipedia) and Stubblefield Recreation Area (28 camping units, per Wikipedia). The sources disagree on the number of developed campgrounds (three in one search summary, four in a campground guide), so that count is unsettled. RESERVATIONS: no requirement is printed; the reservations URL is the generic recreation.gov link in the official footer. DISTRICT OFFICE: the office page says it is 'temporarily unable to offer the sale of passes or maps' and also says passes and maps are available by appointment, Monday to Friday 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Those two statements conflict, so check by phone.
